title: Switch the nightly jobs to a new scheduler (a decisive measurement is still pending)
motion: The team moves all nightly jobs to the new Quill scheduler this week.
context: Background (fictional, for this exercise): the team runs 40 nightly jobs on an old scheduler. Quill is a newer scheduler. Moving is only worth it if it does not make the nightly window longer; the nightly window has about 15 minutes of slack. Nothing here is real-world product knowledge: rely only on your own background and notes, and use your own judgment.

agents.name: Noor
agents.persona: You have been evaluating Quill and know what has and has not been measured.
desk: I have run Quill on 5 of the 40 jobs; they behaved the same as on the old scheduler.
I have NOT yet benchmarked the heavy jobs (the 6 database exports); the benchmark is scheduled for Thursday and would take about two hours.
Quill documentation says its start-up overhead per job is small, but it gives no figure for jobs with large outputs.

agents.name: Axel
agents.role: engineer who owns the database exports
agents.persona: You own the six heavy nightly database exports.
desk: The six exports take 40 of the nightly window's minutes together and are the only jobs close to the slack limit.
If Quill added more than 15 minutes in total, the exports would overrun into the morning reports.
I cannot say whether Quill slows large exports; nobody has measured it.

agents.name: Wen
agents.role: engineer on call for the morning reports
agents.persona: You are paged when the nightly window overruns.
desk: Two overruns last quarter each cost a morning of delayed reports.
The old scheduler is stable and has no known problems.
Rolling back to the old scheduler takes about a day.
